name: Donation Station
shortDescription: A UK contactless-donation kiosk app that uses a church's own tablet, SumUp reader and merchant account for card giving.
suitableContexts: Churches that already have or prefer to buy their own iPad or Android tablet and SumUp reader
Teams seeking a lower-cost contactless giving kiosk without proprietary hardware

pricing.summary: The supplier publishes a £4.99/month Premium plan and states that payment processing uses the church's own SumUp account at SumUp's stated 1.69% fee. The app itself is free to download; confirm current Premium and SumUp charges before purchase.

startingPrice.qualifier: Premium plan; a compatible tablet and SumUp reader are separate requirements

tiers.label: Premium
tiers.detail: Supplier-published in-app purchase; Gift Aid is described as a Premium feature

gdprInformation: The app-store privacy disclosure identifies data types the developer says may be handled. Ask the supplier for the supplier's full privacy terms, processing agreement, hosting or retention terms.
coreFeatures: Contactless, Apple Pay, Google Pay and Chip and PIN
integrations: Google Sheets export for Gift Aid declarations
importExport: App listing describes Google Sheets export for Gift Aid declarations

uk-purchasing.value: Supplier presents Donation Station as UK-based, and Companies House records Donation Station Ltd.

gbp-pricing.value: Supplier site and App Store record a £4.99/month Premium option.

gift-aid.value: Supplier describes digital Gift Aid declarations for UK-registered charities as a Premium feature.

exports.value: Supplier app listing describes exporting Gift Aid declarations to Google Sheets.

editorial.assessment: Donation Station is a lightweight contactless-kiosk model: the church supplies its tablet and connects its own SumUp merchant account, so payment settlement is not mediated by a proprietary hardware rental arrangement. That can be attractive for cost and ownership, but the church must test device management, connectivity, physical placement, SumUp terms, Gift Aid export and the finance hand-off.
bestFor: Churches that want to reuse a tablet and buy their own SumUp reader
Small teams seeking a low-cost contactless kiosk
Churches that prefer donations to settle through their own SumUp account
strengths: Digital Gift Aid and export to Google Sheets are documented
limitations: The church remains responsible for compatible hardware, its SumUp account and device administration
Ask for the privacy, hosting, retention, support and data-processing terms that apply
Gift Aid eligibility and claims still require the church's own controls and review

procurementVerdict.problem: Churches seeking low-cost tablet-based contactless giving
procurementVerdict.differentiator: A church-owned tablet and SumUp account replace proprietary donation hardware
procurementVerdict.firstCheck: Test the complete device, payment, Gift Aid export and reconciliation workflow with the treasurer
